Variance of the Beta Distribution in Two Shapes

Source: R/moments.R
variance.Beta2Distrib.Rd

Closed form: $$\operatorname{Var}(Y) = \frac{\alpha\beta} {(\alpha+\beta)^2(\alpha+\beta+1)}.$$ Writing \(\mu = \alpha/(\alpha+\beta)\) and \(\phi = \alpha+\beta\) this is the \(\mu(1-\mu)/(\phi+1)\) of variance.Beta1Distrib(), so the shapes and the mean-precision pair describe the same law.

Arguments

x

A Beta2Distrib, from beta2_distrib().

theta

A named list with components alpha and beta, both positive, each a numeric vector of length 1 or n. Both shapes below 1 puts the mass at the two endpoints.

...

Unused, and accepted so that the signature matches the generic's.

Value

A numeric vector of variances, of length max(length(theta$alpha), length(theta$beta)).

Notation

\(\alpha > 0\) and \(\beta > 0\) are the two shapes.

See also

mean.Beta2Distrib(), skewness.Beta2Distrib(); variance.Beta1Distrib(); beta2_distrib().

Examples

d <- beta2_distrib()

# The published form, written out.
all.equal(variance(d, list(alpha = 2, beta = 3)), 2 * 3 / (25 * 6))
#> [1] TRUE

# Both shapes 1 is the uniform, of variance 1/12.
all.equal(variance(d, list(alpha = 1, beta = 1)), 1 / 12)
#> [1] TRUE
